title: The icon previews strip reads as previews: no chip looks selected, and it says what it is
goal: The icon previews strip (top left of the canvas when an icon frame is picked, 2026-09-14) draws the icon at 16, 24, 32, 48 and 64 px, and the second biggest sits on a dark ground to show the icon on dark. The user read that dark 48 chip as 'selected', clicked the others, and nothing happened. Make the strip read for what it is: previews at real sizes, light and dark, nothing to pick.
notes: User, 2026-11-04 (intake): 'i see this weird icon preview overlay on the top left ... the preview says we have 48 selected, and if i click on the other options it doesn't change'. Code: Sources/Photonz/IconPreviewsStrip.swift ('the one before the biggest on a dark ground, as icon-draw-wt.html draws it'), IconPreviewsOverlay.swift, EditorState+IconPreviews.swift. The mock icon-draw-wt.html changes with it: an approved departure, update the mock.
acceptance: No chip looks selected: the dark-ground preview is shown as its own clearly labelled pair (each size on light AND on dark, or a Light/Dark toggle for the whole strip), never one chip singled out by a dark plate.

The strip says what it is in a few words ('Actual sizes') and its chips do not look like buttons (no hover lift, no pointer cursor) unless clicking does something; if a click is kept, it does something useful and visible (for example zoom the canvas to show the icon at that size), decided and written down.

MEASURED, and today's strip fails it: in a crop of the strip, every size shows the same grounds as every other size, so the count of dark plates is either zero or one for each size. Today it is one dark plate across five sizes. Pressing a chip changes no pixel of the strip unless a click was kept on purpose.
A short reel and a contact sheet under queue/audits/, named in the audit: the pointer passes over the chips and clicks them, before and after.
It appears only while an icon frame or an icon-sized picture is what you are working in, as today, and never covers the icon itself.
Walk and before/after screenshots in the audit under queue/audits/ (the user's: queue/audits/2026-11-04-ask-icon-confusion.png).
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

digest 2026-11-05: epic moved from image-editing to icon-grid, whose title holds live previews at every size. The focus's success list names this task under PREVIEW.

Reproduced on the probe: icon-previews-dark-chip-walk 2-drawn-sc.png shows one dark plate (32) among four sizes. It also shows what the checklist assumes is not so: the card's lower right corner lies over the frame's top left, so 'never covers the icon' is not true today and a taller card makes it worse. Adversarial review before building: a Light/Dark toggle would be one more thing that looks picked and hides the second ground behind a click, so it is out. Chips stay button-shaped even in pairs, so the plan is two continuous grounds, Light and Dark, each size drawn straight on both, no chip per size. A click on the card still fell through to the canvas and could pick what lies under it, which puts the strip away.
owns these walks: icon-previews-read-as-previews-walk, icon-previews-both-grounds-walk, icon-previews-keep-off-the-icon-walk, icon-previews-stay-with-nothing-picked-walk

Chose two continuous Light and Dark grounds over a pair of chips per size or a Light/Dark toggle, because a chip is what read as a button and a toggle is one more thing that looks picked. Chose a press that does nothing and stops at the card over keeping a click (zoom to that size), because nothing about a real-size preview wants zooming and letting it through could pick something hidden under the card and put the card away.

Measured on real captures, same drawing, 1700 x 1000 window. Dark plates per size: before 16:0 24:0 32:1 48:0, after 16:1 24:1 32:1 48:1. Card pixels changed by a press: 0 at all 6 points after; also 0 at all 5 points before, so that number alone does not separate them. What does: expectClickReaches said every press before reached the picture, and every press after stops on the card, with Ellipse still picked at the end (expectPicked). Bar column script was a one-off in /tmp, not kept.
